statements.quote: We conducted two large pre-registered parallel experiments involving 1,100 participants attempting tasks targeting the two core components of creativity, divergent and convergent thinking.

To answer these questions, we designed and conducted two pre-registered parallel experiments with 1,100 participants that assess how these forms of LLM assistance influence unassisted human creativity, compared to a control group with no AI assistance.

To understand these dynamics, our first pre-registered1 experiment investigates the effects of LLMs that either directly provide ideas or guide participants using a framework, helping them to develop their own ideas.

The items in each round were randomly sampled from five items: tire, pants, shoe, table, bottle.
We measure the originality of each AUT idea with an existing fine-tuned GPT-3 classifier [44].

Following our pre-registration, we conducted a Kruskal-Wallis H test to compare the distribution of originality across the three conditions: None, List of Ideas, and List of Strategies, using a significance level of 0.05.
Based on a power analysis using simulated and pilot data, we determined that this sample size will be necessary to achieve 70% power with a moderate effect size and a significance level of 0.05.

Motivated by this, our second pre-registered2 experiment focuses on convergent thinking, testing not only LLM-generated answers but also the potential of LLMs to guide users toward solutions, simulating a coaching approach.

For the Remote Associates Test (RAT), we employed a widely-used dataset from Bowden and Jung-Beeman [11].

Following our pre-registration, we conducted an Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) to compare the average accuracy between the three conditions in test rounds, controlling for the number of words generated in the verbal fluency task as a covariate.
The sample size was determined through a power analysis using simulated data from pilot studies, ensuring 80% power for the main pre-registered test.

Following our pre-registered analysis plan, the ANCOVA revealed a significant effect of verbal fluency on performance (𝐹(1, 1256) = 16.715, 𝑝< 0.001) as well as a significant main effect of condition (𝐹(2, 1256) = 5.134, 𝑝= 0.006).

notes:
Checked 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without authentication, email, or personal identifiers. Read all 91633 characters (611 lines) of the markdown conversion in contiguous chunks, including the references and Appendices A and B. Checked relevant PDF pages and all external hyperlink annotations. The saved PDF has 18 pages and is arXiv:2410.03703v2, dated 15 February 2025. The public arXiv landing page, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03703, returned HTTP 200 and still identifies v2 as the latest revision. Quotes come from PDF text, with line wrapping and line-end word hyphenation normalized; the superscript preregistration footnote digits are retained inline in two quotations. Statements include preregistration mentions, material locations/provenance, and scoring-API access, none of which promises public release of the study data. No formal data/code availability statement, on-request offer, study-data repository, or separate online supplementary-file URL was found. The form data_and_code.data_url and code_url are both empty.

The two confirmed public deposits contain preregistrations only. The paper itself provides task-interface illustrations (Figures 3 and 8), GPT-4o settings and input/system prompts (Appendices A.1 and B.1; Figures 11 and 12), and illustrative LLM stimuli (Tables 1 and 2). These are materials, not linked participant records. The acknowledged Organisciak scoring API is an upstream scoring tool, not a deposit of these experiments. No participant or output table could be read, so rows_checked and columns_checked are null. No public data were confirmed that permit computation of the missing analyzed/per-arm counts, participant means, SDs or SEs, participant-clustered accuracy/originality estimates, or participant-aware individual/group diversity measures in final.open_items. The unit-of-analysis, Tukey-adjustment, Monte Carlo sampling, guidance-contamination, and creative-flexibility Exposure-set questions remain unresolved. The preregistrations document intended procedures, not realized exclusions or analyses.

The DataCite searches found the article rather than a separate data deposit. As an additional check, https://arxiv.org/src/2410.03703 returned HTTP 200, application/gzip, filename arXiv-2410.03703v2.tar.gz, 9642932 bytes. The archive was inspected entirely in memory and all 28 non-directory members were enumerated: manuscript TeX, bibliography/style files, README.txt for the ACM typesetting class, and PNG figure images. No CSV, spreadsheet, participant JSON, analysis notebook/script, or ancillary raw-data file was present. The manuscript TeX contains the same two AsPredicted links and no study-data release link. main.tex line 375 contains approximate narrative descriptions of Figure 4 means and error-bar widths; those are aggregate figure descriptions and cannot recover participant distributions or defensible SEs. This manuscript-source archive and the arXiv article are not counted as separate data deposits.

Publisher checks: https://doi.org/10.1145/3706598.3714198 redirected to https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3706598.3714198 and ended at HTTP 403; a direct request to the same ACM landing page also returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare Just a moment bot-check page. Stopped there without attempting to bypass it. Publisher supplementary files and the version-of-record comparison could not be checked. The failure does not establish that a dataset requires an account or approval, so the overall status is not restricted. This limitation and the title-only scope of the specified OSF nodes endpoint support medium confidence. No relevant OSF, Dataverse, or Zenodo deposit was identified that required a file-listing API call. No study GitHub repository is named in the paper, and no GitHub API requests were made.

Other paper/PDF links checked: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06292 (reference [39]) and https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04109 (reference [55]) both returned HTTP 200 and are other papers. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06792-0 (reference [10]) returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to Nature, but its body was a Client Challenge; stopped. https://doi.org/10.1145/3613904.3642105 (reference [46]) returned HTTP 403 at ACM with a bot check; stopped. The four author-profile annotations, https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2878-3986, https://orcid.org/0009-0007-2443-1576, https://orcid.org/0009-0001-3176-5036, and https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3089-6883, each returned HTTP 200 with an ORCID HTML page. These references/profiles are not study-data deposits. Registration archive mirrors are recorded with their parent deposits.
